pk.context: 40 mg once daily delayed-release capsules, day 5, adults with symptomatic GERD

pill.desc: amethyst, opaque, hard gelatin capsule with yellow radial bars on the cap

clues.title: Approval
clues.text: Approved by FDA in February 2001 as 20 and 40 mg delayed-release capsules. A packet for oral suspension followed in 2006.

clues.title: Sponsor and strengths
clues.text: Held by AstraZeneca. Strengths run from 2.5 mg packets for infants up to 40 mg capsules.

clues.title: Class
clues.text: A proton pump inhibitor, marketed as the pure S-isomer of an earlier racemic drug from the same company.

clues.title: Mechanism
clues.text: Protonated in the acidic compartment of the parietal cell, it forms an achiral sulphenamide that inhibits H⁺/K⁺ ATPase, the final step of acid production.

clues.title: Drug substance
clues.text: A magnesium salt of the S-isomer, a trihydrate of (C₁₇H₁₈N₃O₃S)₂Mg·3H₂O, MW 767.2. It is stable at alkaline pH but degrades rapidly in acid.

clues.title: Capsule
clues.text: Opaque amethyst hard capsules holding enteric-coated granules, with two yellow radial bars on the cap at 20 mg and three at 40 mg.

clues.title: Exposure
clues.text: At 40 mg daily, bioavailability rises from 64% after one dose to about 90% at steady state, because the drug autoinhibits CYP2C19. Food cuts AUC by 43 to 53%.

clues.title: Nonclinical
clues.text: Rat carcinogenicity studies of its racemate produced gastric ECL cell carcinoids. In people, ECL hyperplasia increases with dose and time but no carcinoids were seen.

clues.title: Warnings
clues.text: Warnings include acute tubulointerstitial nephritis, C. difficile diarrhea, fracture, hypomagnesemia and B12 deficiency. Contraindicated with rilpivirine.

clues.title: Indications
clues.text: Indicated for erosive esophagitis, GERD symptoms, NSAID ulcer risk reduction, H. pylori eradication and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
